card.name: Babukung
card.era: Traditional ritual; Babukung Festival staged since 2014
card.tagline: Masked Dayak Tomun funeral dance accompanying the soul
card.profile: Babukung is a funeral ritual masked dance of the Kaharingan religion practiced by the Dayak Tomun of Lamandau Regency, Central Kalimantan (Wikipedia). When a community member dies, masked dancers called Bukung come from neighboring villages wearing 'luha' masks representing animals and spirits to comfort the bereaved family, dispel evil spirits and honor the deceased's soul. The Babukung Festival has been officially recognized by the Lamandau Regency Government since 2014, using 15 mask categories including bird, dragon, crocodile, bat, hornbill, peacock, dog, butterfly and the white-faced 'sadap' mask (GuidepostTours).
card.insight: Wearing the luha mask symbolizes the dancer's transformation from human into spirit, bridging the living and the dead in Kaharingan belief (Indonesia.travel).
